title: Batcher intermittent silence and fairness runbook
creator: Priya Menon
description: This ticket captures the follow-up work from a recurring class of incidents where the continuous batcher intermittently enters a multi-second 'silence' state for a subset of slots and tenants, causing long-tail latency spikes and observed fairness regressions. The incident was first noticed in production during a capacity churn window and amplified by a telemetry blind spot. This doc is a runbook + action item list to close telemetry gaps, harden the coalescer, add rapid remediation controls, and implement fairness guardrails that survive autoscaler events.
timeline:
2026-03-09T22:14Z: alerts for p99 generation latency > 2s from multiple canaries in us-west-2.
2026-03-09T22:18Z: oncall paging, initial mitigation: scale up pool -> no immediate effect.
2026-03-09T22:30Z: manual probe showed batch formation timers for ~12% of slots not firing for 1.5-3s.
2026-03-09T22:45Z: rollback of a recent coalescer timer micro-optimization (rev: rfd-3319) reduced incidence immediately.
2026-03-10: post-incident triage discovered missing heartbeat metric (coalescer_heartbeat_missed_total) in our primary dashboard; gaps in slot-level tracing for ~6 hours around the event window.
impact_summary: Incidents affected ~14% of requests in the impacted pool during the window, causing p95->p99 jumps and ~40k extra tokens billed due to retries. Two downstream customers reported visible latency regressions; internal SLO burn estimated at 3.4% for that day in the affected region.
root_cause: A recent optimization intended to reduce timer wakeups changed coalescer scheduling so that under slot churn (autoscaler + driver restarts) certain slots lost a soft-lease renewal path. The code path relied on a racey fast-path where slot timers would be rearmed by a background ticker; when autoscaler reclaimed and reattached workers, the rearm didn't occur for ~1-3s. This exposed a secondary telemetry gap: slot-level heartbeats and batch formation time-series were not being emitted for detached slots, so the operator view showed capacity returning even though some slots were silent. Together these caused localized batch desertion and priority inversion for small, low-throughput tenants queued behind long-running ones.
mitigations_taken_immediate: Rolled back coalescer fast-path micro-optimization (rfd-3319) -> reduced incidence within 8 minutes
Activated emergency per-pool conservative batching (forced max-wait 12ms) for impacted clusters
Opened high-cardinality trace capture for a rotating subset of slots to collect full stack traces for next 48 hours
action_items: (Ethan) Add explicit slot_lease_renewal metric + coalescer_heartbeat_missed_total by 2026-03-20 (estimate: 3)
(Marta) Instrument batch_formation_latency_ms and publish deciles to console and pager thresholds (estimate: 2)
(Ravi) Implement fallback rearm path: when a slot detects >1 missed tick, schedule a guaranteed rearm on a separate control thread (estimate: 5)
(Priya) Deploy an autoscaler-aware admission control that temporarily enforces per-tenant soft-concurrency caps during pool churn (estimate: 4)
(SRE) Create runbook automation to detect coalescer silence and perform a rolling control-thread restart before escalation (estimate: 2)
(QE) Add synthetic scenario in integration tests that simulates autoscaler detach/reattach under high token-velocity and validate no >500ms batch formation gaps (estimate: 3)
followups: Review telemetry retention and alert thresholds with Console team to ensure slot-level metrics are surfaced in the first responder dashboard
Schedule a canary for the fallback rearm path across 3% of traffic for 72 hours before wide rollout
Post-deploy eval: measure p95/p99 and fairness delta across tenants using the new metrics for 7 days
Consolidate lessons into a short postmortem + publish to ops handbook
notes: This incident class has been appearing intermittently at low frequency; many prior docs focus on queue starvation in steady-state. The unique amplifier here was the interaction with autoscaler churn plus a telemetry blind spot. Priority for follow-ups is to close the observability loop and add a small, deterministic fallback (guaranteed rearm) that avoids large changes to steady-state performance. We should avoid repeating previous fixes that only mask symptoms; aim for an approach that is observable, testable, and reversible.
